question: Does restricting complete-supervision fitting to publicly defined no-strong pairs improve conditional Chinese seller-alias ranking?
selection: Reuse the old M3-joint grid selected using training-only grouped OOF AP. No new tuning, validation fit, early stopping, weighting, sampling, or probability calibration.
primary: no_strong development world-equal AP(no_strong arm)-AP(all arm)

operating_point.role: Evaluation-only ROC characteristic, using evaluation labels; not a deployable threshold or independent calibration guarantee.

decision: Further investigation only if primary paired 95% lower bound > 0 and pooled no-strong recall at empirical FPR <= 1% is not lower. Otherwise stop this fixed-input fixed-capacity restriction candidate; do not infer that all public information is unlearnable.
limits: Exploratory reused-development evidence, not an independent confirmatory test.
Both arms get the same model capacity and hyperparameters; row counts and label priors intentionally differ. Equal tree counts are not equal FLOPs.
Restriction also changes fitted bins and automatic initial class prior; it does not isolate an easy-example gradient suppression mechanism.
Old train-only hyperparameters were selected for the all arm; a negative result does not reject all tuned specialist models.
Shared imputation uses all public training rows without labels, including rows excluded from specialist fitting.
No-strong selection uses only two public feature columns. It never consumes a private mechanism, controller, positive quota or test label.
The specialist is evaluated conditionally. Its full-population output is extrapolative descriptive evidence, not a routed deployment.
No English data, raw text re-encoding, Audit A/B truth or predictions, Linux access, or changes to old experiments.
